parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Calcium carbonate is heated in a closed container. CaCO 3 CaO + CO 2

ms.label: 5(a)(iv)
ms.text:
limewater (1)
turns milky / goes cloudy / white precipitate (1)

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Carbon dioxide is produced when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with calcium carbonate. CaCO 3 + 2HC l → CaC l 2 + CO 2 + H 2 O

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Complete the diagram to show the apparatus used to investigate the volume of carbon dioxide produced during this reaction. [2]

ms.label: 5(b)(i)
ms.text:
flask or other suitable container (1)
connecting tubing AND apparatus gas-tight / no air gaps (1)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Describe the effect of each of the following on the rate of reaction of dilute hydrochloric acid with calcium carbonate. ● The temperature is decreased. All other conditions stay the same. ............................................................................................................................................. ● Calcium carbonate powder is used instead of large pieces of calcium carbonate. All other conditions stay the same. ............................................................................................................................................. [2]

ms.label: 5(b)(ii)
ms.text:
lower temperature: (rate) decreases / (rate) lower (1) / (rate) slower
powdered CaCO3: (rate) increases / (rate) higher (1) / (rate) faster

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Carbon dioxide is also formed when the hydrocarbon C 4 H 8 is completely combusted.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) The hydrocarbon C 4 H 8 is an alkene. Complete the structure of this alkene by adding the missing bonds and atom. [2]

ms.label: 5(c)(i)
ms.text:
double bond between 3rd and 4th C atoms from left (1)
─ H connected to 4th carbon from the left (1)

ms.label: 5(c)(ii)
ms.text: (combustion with) limited oxygen / the hydrocarbon is in excess (1)
